claim: nats-server issue #8787 (open, defect, 2026-10-21): an embedded nats-server v2.14.0 running as a spoke leaf crashed out of memory after about 7.4 days; the reporter traces it to the leaf-node permission check caching subjects that alias the read buffer, giving unbounded Sublist cache growth
nats-server issue #6902 (open, defect, 2025-05-19): ACLs cannot grant only domain-mapped JetStream API subjects such as JS.cloud.API.> because permissions are checked against the real path JS.API.>
nats-server issue #2949 (open since 2022-03-24): 'Allow Responses' user permission does not transit a leaf connection, blocking service replies
rancher/fleet issue #594 (open since 2021-11-05, kind/bug, area/rollout): if any clusters are offline, the status of bundles deployed to them can get stuck with misleading error messages

rancher/fleet issues #2891 (2024, 'How do partitions work?') and #3586 (closed 2025-07-02, 'Document and test more advanced rollout behaviour') show users asking how to make a failed partition block the next one and whether an offline cluster fails a partition

headscale PR #3156 (open, performance, 2026-03-24): a CTF team serving thousands of participants reports 'the current version of Headscale cannot handle it, primarily due to the O(N^2) reachability computation of each node to each node'

The Register (2025-05-02): the CNCF-Synadia dispute stemmed from Synadia's plan to move NATS code from 'Apache 2.0 to Business Source License (BSL) in future releases'; it was settled with Synadia assigning its two NATS trademark registrations to the Linux Foundation and the NATS.io domain and GitHub repositories staying with CNCF under Apache-2.0; Synadia had not said whether it would still pursue BSL

ROS 2 Kilted Kaiju (May 2025) is the first ROS 2 release with Eclipse Zenoh (rmw_zenoh_cpp) as a Tier 1 middleware; Fast DDS remains the default RMW in Kilted and, per a ROS PMC post (May 2026), in Lyrical; the ROS 2 robotics ecosystem converged on DDS/Zenoh, not NATS (search-result summaries of docs.ros.org and openrobotics.org; pages not opened individually)

Tschirschnitz et al., 'Method Confusion Attack on Bluetooth Pairing' (IEEE S&P, May 2021): two devices can be made to pair with differing methods so a man-in-the-middle can 'intercept all traffic'; in a 40-person user study 'none of the 40 participants noticed the ongoing attack' and 37 (92.5 %) completed pairing

GitHub contributors API on 2026-11-12: the go-fdo library's top human contributors have 18, 6, 2, 2, 1 and 1 commits (concentrated in one person), with 26 commits since 2026-05-12; go-fdo-server's top human contributors have 120, 57, 53, 46, 43 and 19 commits, with 34 commits since 2026-05-12 and Red Hat edge-team ticket references in PR titles (e.g. THEEDGE-4639)

Rancher Fleet published six security advisories in 2026-09/10, including GHSA-qfmw-gw96-ffcr (critical: privilege escalation to cluster-admin on the local cluster through the agent-management controller; patched 0.16.3), GHSA-gx8v-2929-9q95 (high: cluster identity takeover in cluster registration giving access to another cluster's Fleet namespace; patched 0.16.3) and GHSA-h9p5-fp5h-qpqr (high: cross-tenant BundleDeployment and Secret disclosure via spoofed cluster labels during agent-initiated registration; patched v0.16.1); the lab's v0.16.3 is the patched release

nats-server security advisories published 2026-06-29 include GHSA-qrcv-3558-gj4f (high: MQTT SUBSCRIBE protocol injection via leaf-node/route forwarding allows arbitrary NATS command injection; patched 2.14.1/2.12.9), GHSA-3g5q-cfh2-cq67 (high: pre-auth crash via double INFO in the leafnode handshake, incomplete fix of CVE-2026-29785; patched 2.12.8/2.11.17), GHSA-7qmq-8cc4-hxwg (MQTT retained/QoS replay bypasses subscribe deny filters; patched 2.14.3/2.12.12) and GHSA-p3j5-5hrq-p75h (leaf connections bypass a Nats-Trace-Dest permission check)
